source.howDecided: In src/caldiy: `git log --format='%h %ad %s' --date=short 038381aeca..origin/main -- <culprit files>` returned nothing. The whole delta 038381aeca..176037d0af is 4 commits (#29819 Clara app, #29740 phone-input country fallback, #29901 language update, #29940 customReplyToEmail) and `git diff --stat 038381aeca origin/main` lists 16 files, none of them a culprit file for this finding. I then read the culprit region out of today's head with `git show origin/main:<file>` and re-numbered it: the lines are byte-identical to the tested tree and sit at the same line numbers. At head lines 123-150 still read "// === Stubs for deleted EE features still imported by API v2 ===", "// Round-robin reassignment removed (EE feature) - stubs for API v2", and both roundRobinManualReassignment (126-138) and roundRobinReassignment (140-150) still have `// No-op in community edition` as their entire body, while the four sibling stubs below them (createApiKeyHandler at 153 onward) still throw "not available in community edition".

queries: gh search issues --owner calcom --include-prs --limit 30 --updated '>2026-04-15' 'reassign'  (11 hits, all other subjects: calendar credential removal #29978, oauth open redirect #29681, calcom/help#151 reassignment-notification docs, RR idempotency key #26031, host groups #26519, signup refactors; none about the community-edition no-op or the reassign response)

gh search issues --owner calcom --include-prs --limit 30 '"community edition"'  (6 hits, none about the EE stubs: cal.diy#29898, cal.diy#29688, cal.diy#28888 self-hosting docs, cal.diy#1172, cal.diy#6221, calcom/docker#156)

reevaluation: Stands unchanged, high confidence. packages/platform/libraries/index.ts is untouched, so both reassign routes still await an empty async function and still answer 200 {status: success, data: {bookingUid, reassignedTo}} naming the host the booking already had, for every booking, in about 20 to 30 ms with no log line and no email. No one has reported it: nothing about the EE stubs or the reassign endpoints has appeared since the fork. The one thing re-check does not change, and which the filer MUST carry over, is the review's correction of the scenario's premise. The scenario reassignment-refuses-a-non-round-robin-booking asserts that a non-round-robin booking must be refused; the pre-fork implementation had no schedulingType gate at all and would have accepted that same call, so "the docs say non-round-robin must be refused" is not a supportable claim. The defect is the other one: on Cal.diy the endpoint can never do anything, for any booking, and reports success anyway, which contradicts the tested tree's own @ApiOperation and its ReassignBookingOutput DTO, and breaks the fork's own convention, since the four sibling stubs in the same file throw "not available in community edition".
policyBasis: calcom/cal.diy .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml sets `blank_issues_enabled: false`, so a bug must go through bug_report.md (Issue Summary / Steps to Reproduce / Actual Results / Expected Results / Technical details / Evidence, the last called "quite mandatory in terms of bugs"); CONTRIBUTING.md: "For bugs, security, performance, documentation, etc., you can start coding immediately, even if the `needs approval` label is present", so no discussion-first gate applies.
notes: This is a Cal.diy-only defect created by the fork commit ab21c7f805 (PR #28903 "refactor: Cal.diy"), so it must be filed on calcom/cal.diy and must NOT be phrased as a cal.com bug: the commercial product still ships the real round-robin engine. The one-line ask is to make the two stubs throw like their four siblings (or unregister the routes / answer 501), never to return success. Of the two scenarios behind this finding only reassignment-refuses-a-non-round-robin-booking.api.1 carries it; the sibling reassign-a-round-robin-booking.api.1 was ruled test-defect (it asserted data.uid and data.hosts[0].id, fields no schema on either doc page defines) and must not be cited as evidence. That sibling did surface a separate, genuine DOC defect worth a second issue: the NestJS envelope class and the platform-types data class are both named ReassignBookingOutput_2024_08_13, so Nest's Swagger plugin collapses them and the published OpenAPI $refs the envelope from its own data property, leaving the reassign pages documenting zero response fields, and the prose still names ReassignAutoBookingOutput / ReassignManualBookingOutput, which exist nowhere in the codebase. Step 3 (the auto route) never ran, but roundRobinReassignment is the identical no-op. calcom/cal.com and calcom/cal.diy are the SAME repository: gh api repos/calcom/cal.com returns full_name calcom/cal.diy (the repo was renamed, GitHub redirects the old path). Every calcom/cal.com#NNNN reference in the review resolves to the same number on calcom/cal.diy, and one `--owner calcom` search covers both. The commercial Cal.com source is private, so nothing about the hosted product is verifiable and no "fixed in cal.com" claim can be made.
